 Judgment

These three appeals are preferred by the insurance company challenging the common judgment and award passed by the VI Additional Judge Court of Small Causes, MACT at Bengaluru City dated 1.3.2014 in MVC Nos.8535/2010, 8536/2010 and 8537/2010.

sentences.text: These appeals are premised on the ground that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is illegal, perverse and hence to set aside the same.
2. The parties shall be referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 26.9.2010 at about 03.00 p.m., the claimant (in MVC No.8537/2010), one Prabhakar, was riding the motor cycle bearing registration No.CKS 2720 with his friends viz. Upendrakumar and Harish as pillion riders.

While they were so proceeding on the motor cycle on Bangalore ring road, near Sumanahalli Road so as to go to Laggare at Kempegowdanagar, at that time, a lorry bearing registration No.KA-05-B-3050 belonging to respondent No.1, driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner at high speed so as to endanger human life, dashed against the motor cycle ridden by Prabhakar thereby causing serious injuries to the rider as well as two pillion riders.

Due to the accident, the rider i.e.,Prabhakar and New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Sri.Narayanappa on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69794755/
5 two pillion riders fell down from the bike but unfortunately, one of the pillion rider, Sri Upendra Kumar came under the wheels of the lorry and died on the spot.

sentences.text: Accordingly, three claim petitions came to be filed; one by the legal representatives of the deceased Upendra Kumar and two claim petitions by the injured rider and the pillion rider.

4. Respondent No.1, owner of the offending vehicle i.e., the lorry in all the three cases remained absent and was placed exparte and respondent No.2- Insurance Company filed detailed objection statement inter alia denying the contentions of the claim petition and objecting to the averments with regard to the claim and pleaded that the compensation claimed was exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the claim petitions as per the grounds urged in the objection statement.
5.
Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
In order to substantiate their case, the claimants examined themselves as PWs 1 to 5 and also got examined doctors as PWs 6 and 7.
They got marked exhibits P1 to P34 in support of their cases.
The respondent No.2- Insurance Company examined its officer as RW1 and got marked exhibits R1 to R3 in support of its case.

6. On the basis of the material evidence, both oral and documentary, the Tribunal partly allowed all the three claim petitions and awarded compensation of Rs.3,75,000/- in MVC No.8535/2010,
Rs.2,16,120/- in MVC No.8536/2010 and Rs.2,54,900/- in MVC No.8537/2010.

7. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the Insurance Company is in appeal questioning the judgment and award of the Tribunal mainly on the ground that there is contributory negligence on behalf of the rider of the motor cycle who was riding the motor cycle along with two pillion riders which is in violation of terms and conditions of the policy so also against the Motor Vehicle Act and the Rules.

It is the further contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the rider of the motor cycle is responsible for the occurrence of the accident as he was not diligent and he was carrying an extra person as a pillion rider in the motor cycle and being unable to control the vehicle, has contributed to the occurrence of the accident.

Therefore, he contends - 10 - that the very fact that there were two pillion riders apart from the rider itself pre-supposes that an inference has to be drawn that there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor which has been ignored and given a go-by by the Tribunal.
On this sole ground the present appeal is filed attributing contributory negligence as against the rider of the motor cycle.

It is the further contention of the Learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the tribunal has failed to attribute contributory negligence and the same requires to be attributed against the rider of the motor cycle and thereby the judgment and award accordingly will have be modified and hence he seeks to allow this appeal.
8.

Per contra, Sri R Jaiprakash, Learned counsel representing the claimants vehemently opposed the contentions put forth by the Insurance Company and contends that the rider of the motor cycle, of New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Sri.Narayanappa on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69794755/
6 course,
- 11 - was traveling with two pillion riders which is not a disputed fact but the fact remains is that the FIR and charge sheet has been laid against the driver of the lorry which is not questioned and challenged and there is no FIR or charge sheet filed against the rider of the motor cycle for violating the terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly contributed the entire negligence on the part of the owner of the lorry and the Insurance company in view of a subsisting policy for the said lorry has been rightly fastened with the liability to make good the compensation in favour of the claimants, which does not call for interference and he therefore, contends that the appeal does not merit any consideration and the same deserves to be dismissed.

9. Having heard the Learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company and the claimants, the - 12 - points that arise for consideration before this Court are:
i) Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has made out any good ground to interfere with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal?
ii) Whether the same requires modification?
iii) What order?
10. Having perused the entire materials placed before this Court and having gone through the impugned judgment and award, the only point for consideration is whether there is any contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle in causation or occurrence of the accident?

I am afraid that the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant-insurer cannot be accepted as there is no cogent material placed on record to the contributory negligence as against the rider of the motor cycle.

Merely for the reason that along with the rider, two - 13 - pillion riders were traveling on the motor cycle, I do not find any good ground to interfere with the well reasoned judgment passed by the Tribunal for the reasons stated below.
11. The occurrence of the accident, involvement of the vehicles, injuries sustained and death having occurred due to the accident are all not disputed.
The same is accepted and not questioned.

Hence,
this Court would not delve into the correctness of the aspects as they are all admitted and proved by the claimants by production of exhibits P1 to P34.
The policy being in force is also not in dispute as the respondent-Insurance Company themselves have admitted the policy and filed Ex.R2, being the policy.

sentences.text: The short point for discussion before this Court is, whether the rider of the motor cycle travelling with two other pillion riders would amount to contributory - 14 - negligence to the occurrence and causation of the accident?

13. In the present case, the Insurance Company has not placed any material before the Court either by way of oral or documentary evidence or by way of elicitation by way of cross examination that the rider of the motor cycle has contributed to the occurrence of the accident which is in violation of the motor vehicle Rules and Regulations leading to the death of one of the pillion rider and injuries to the rider himself as well as another pillion rider.

When there being no such material either by way of documentary or oral evidence, this Court cannot presume there is negligence as against the rider of the motor cycle merely for the reason that the rider of the motor cycle was traveling along with two pillion riders on the fateful day of occurrence of accident, on which day, one of the - 15 - pillion rider met with gruesome fatal injuries and succumbed to death.

14. Time and again, this Court and the Hon'ble Apex Court have laid down the law that merely in violation of the Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations, pillion riders not having proper, valid license or traveling with the learner's license would not amount to contributory negligence unless the Insurance Company makes out a cogent case with material evidence to show that the rider has contributed to the occurrence of the accident and in the present case, no such material having been placed and the charge sheet and FIR having laid against the driver of the offending vehicle lorry, it cannot be presumed or assumed that the rider has contributed to the occurrence of the accident.

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion that negligence is attributed to the driver of the lorry which has caused the accident - 16 - having hit the two wheeler from behind leading to the death of one of the pillion riders and injuries to the rider and another pillion rider.
I am afraid the contentions put forth by the Insurance Company cannot be accepted as there is no merit in the submissions put forth by the Insurance Company.
